hero.subhead: I write production software with agents in the loop, ship developer tools at the model boundary, and bring teams that haven't gotten there yet across the line.

home.workBody: Not a productivity hack. The way the work gets built. Years of shipping production software end-to-end mean the AI-augmented work I do becomes product, not demos. I've led an engineering organization through AI tooling adoption end to end: evaluation, rollout, training, and the harder part of moving the engineers who weren't going to come along on their own. I build at the model boundary too, including production MCP tooling for the agents I work with day to day.
home.thinkTitle: From the system, not the pattern.
home.thinkBody: I reach for the underlying mechanism before I reach for prior art. When a system is unfamiliar, I'd rather study it from the foundations than copy a shape that worked somewhere else. On my own time I read papers and build cognitive architectures from scratch, partly because I want to understand the systems I'm shipping at a layer below the API. I bring the same discipline to my own code: every pull request on my main project gets reviewed against a written architectural document before it merges.

sylphie.title: Sylphie
sylphie.summary: A non-LLM-in-the-runtime-path cognitive architecture. Dual-process reasoning, drive-driven attention, language as voice box rather than thinker.

memory-pkg.title: memory-pkg
memory-pkg.summary: Agents forget the work between sessions. memory-pkg indexes every transcript into TimescaleDB and trigram-searches the right history into the next prompt — pure SQL, no LLM in the hot path.

sylphie-pkg.title: sylphie-pkg
sylphie-pkg.summary: Coding agents waste context re-reading files. sylphie-pkg compiles the source tree into a Neo4j graph and serves it over MCP — a map for the agent, not a flashlight.

enforcement-hooks.title: Enforcement Hooks
enforcement-hooks.summary: Agents that grade their own work ship drift. Two hooks — line-level on every write, intent-level at every Stop — keep the agent in lock step with the project's standards.

career.title: Career
career.intro: Eight years senior frontend, four at Mediavine, pivoting into AI.

about.title: About.
about.body1: I make the engineering team I join better than it was before I joined. Half of that is patience: pairing with the engineer who hasn't found their AI workflow yet, writing the rollout doc nobody wants to own, taking the meeting where you explain to the skeptic why this isn't a fad. I led that work end-to-end at my last company and watched the team's ceiling rise as a result.
about.body2: The other half is discipline. I review every pull request on my main project against a written architectural document before it merges, and I bring the same standard to whatever team I'm on, starting with my own code. I reason from a system's mechanism before I reach for prior art. Engineers feel the floor rise around them. That's the value.
